score:f5.notes: All four required files are present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), with the scripts and outputs the memo names beside them (95 dumps in docs/, fetched.tsv, census_out.txt, archival_*.txt, vec_baselines.txt, nn_run1/2.txt, vecops_out.txt, vecjoin_out.txt). checks/ was read only for match_check.txt, o2p_flags.txt, figures_check.txt and style.json and nothing in it is credited to the session; tally_run.md names a model and was ignored. Independent verification against the read-only index copy, the bundle JSON and the vector artifacts: the canary, the 77-volume 38,059 denominator, the corpus counts 0 / 785 / 211, M11 (11; 427|427), M10 (11 of 698 series with y0 < 1940), the 711-document slice and its 392 pointers on 200 documents (exact), the lot -> NAID resolutions, seven quotations, the fourteen numbered steps in d177 and the '28 top leaders' in d484, the provenance digest across index/binary/map/manifest/.generation/553 shards, documentOffset 0.40, and the 82-neighbour pool (no Ed2) all reproduce. The one factual gap: 14 of the 785 `soft AND power` documents are in the two Ed2 volumes whose first editions are in the corpus, and the session's Ed2 statements cover only the 77-volume scope and the 31-document set (S5). Judgement calls an adjudicator may weigh differently: O2 is violated on the decade figures being rates with the counts deferred to the memo ('about one in seventy ... the exact counts ... are in the memo') and on 'one or two capitals' having no memo line; O2' is violated on six number-words with no trace row ('59', 'two channels', 'Two of the documents', 'five findings', 'one or two capitals'), with the script's '103'/'47' and 'A1 1583B' read as traced; V8 is obeyed on the item's enumerated terms although the overview says 'nearest neighbours' without a distance; V1 is obeyed on the digests named as equal although the shards manifest and .generation were not themselves named; S3 is obeyed on the family-level and form-level splits although acronym-versus-spelled-out splits within a family are not reported; R3's entry-number search shows no positive control of its own. The sqlite3 loop I first ran for the M7 rows mis-split its arguments under zsh and printed nothing; the rows were re-queried in Python and match archival_cameFrom.txt. No file under the run directory or the index copy was written; my scratch scripts live under the session scratchpad.

refute:f5.fabricationDetails: None. The 69 checked are the 30 passages the overview sets in quotation marks and attributes to a document (18 full bullet quotations and 12 short prose quotations, counting each occurrence; six passages appear twice, once in prose and once in a bullet) plus the 39 excerpts in the collection. Each was lower-cased, stripped to [a-z0-9], split at ellipses (none has one) and required in order in header||dateline||source_note||body_text of the exact (volume_id, document_id) the memo's trace table gives (refuter/quote_check.py): 30 of 30 and 39 of 39 pass. The other 9 quoted strings in overview.md are not quotations from documents: the search terms "soft power" (x3), "public diplomacy"/"Public diplomacy" (x2), the control "Department of State", the question's word "policymakers", and the stemming example words "clearing"/"clear". Two one-word quotations carry no citation: "Orientals" is found in exactly one of the 31 documents (frus1961-63v04/d81, memo Q19); "face" is a common word found in 16 of the 31 (checked against memo Q16, frus1961-63v02/d16, where it means the face the GVN presents, not 'loss of face'), so the overview's belief claim about sensitivity to "face" rests on no quotation in the set.
refute:f5.miscitationDetails: None. Every bullet quotation sits under a full edition citation with a URL that resolves to the pair in which the words are found. Every short prose quotation is found in exactly one of the 31 collection documents, the one the memo's trace names, and the overview's own description (date, author or office) matches that document (e.g. 'in 1954 the Department refused an "Asia for Asians" theme' = frus1952-54v12p2/d352, 13 Feb 1954; 'In 1970 the agency's first program memorandum' = frus1917-72PubDipv08/d99, 30 July 1970). Fourteen of the 15 URL-cited documents are returned by a substantive logged query (a scope MATCH term such as USIA/USIS/propaganda/"information program", the union-by-volume query, the header LIKE query, a NEAR query, scan.py's A>=2&R>=2 or Adistinct>=2&R>=2 filters, or the PubDip regex filter R>=8 or hR>=1). The fifteenth, frus1977-80v22/d104 (the memo's claimed vector-only document), is returned by NO substantive query (scan.py scored it A=0, B=0, Adistinct=0; no MATCH term, union, LIKE or NEAR returns it) but IS returned by the logged positive-control predicate MATCH '"Department of State"' (log line 46; its header; 15,174 of the 38,059 scope documents match) and lies inside the memo's scope set. reach.method: The 15 URL-cited pairs were taken from the overview's historicaldocuments URLs (all resolve directly; no printed citation needed manifest.json). For each, refuter/reach_check.py re-ran as membership tests every logged full-text predicate: the 20 scope MATCH terms of lines 10-49, the union of line 50, the header LIKE of line 52, the two FTS5 NEAR queries of lines 72-73 (the NEAR/12 query of line 71 is FTS3 syntax FTS5 rejects), the Japan-volume MATCH of line 74, the corpus-wide MATCH predicates (lines 11-49 odd, 93-98), and the regex passes as the session filtered them (scan.py rows with A>=2&R>=2 and Adistinct>=2&R>=2 from scan_docs.tsv; the PubDip rows with R>=8 or hR>=1 from pubdip_scan.tsv, whose columns I identified by recomputing scan.py's families: len, R, hR, A, C, D). STRICT = at least one such predicate returns the document; PRACTICAL = from the log order and file timestamps (stat, to the second), whether the document was in a result set the session had printed or saved before a neighbour list surfaced it. The same tests were run for the six documents quoted without a URL (reach_check_uncited.py): all six are returned by substantive logged queries.
